title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
title_zh: 连接组模拟识别出果蝇行走的中央模式发生器
abstract: Animal locomotion relies on rhythmic body movements driven by central pattern generators (CPGs): neural circuits that produce oscillating output without oscillating input. However, the circuit structure of a CPG for walking is not known in any animal1,2. To identify the cells and synapses that underlie rhythmic leg movement in walking flies, we developed dynamic simulations of the Drosophila ventral nerve cord connectomes3–6. A computational activation screen of descending neurons from the central brain identified DNg100—a known command neuron for walking—as the strongest driver of rhythmic leg motor activity. Simulated network pruning isolated a minimal rhythm-generating circuit consisting of one inhibitory and two excitatory interneurons; this three-neuron circuit was necessary and sufficient for motor rhythms across all six legs and in four connectome datasets. Simulations also predicted that a separate descending pathway (DNb08) drives rhythmic leg movements, which we confirmed experimentally using optogenetics in behaving flies. Our results reveal the cellular identity and synaptic structure of a putative CPG circuit for walking and other rhythmic leg movements in flies. Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking.
abstract_zh: 动物 locomotion 依赖于中央模式发生器（CPGs）驱动的节奏性身体运动，CPG 是能在没有振荡输入的情况下产生振荡输出的神经电路。然而，步行 CPG 的电路结构在任何动物中均未知。为识别行走果蝇中节奏性腿部运动的细胞和突触，我们开发了 Drosophila 腹侧神经索连接组的动态模拟。中央脑下行神经元的计算激活筛选将 DNg100（一种已知的步行指令神经元）确定为驱动节奏性腿部运动神经活动的最强因子。模拟网络修剪分离出一个最小节奏产生电路，该电路由一个抑制性神经元和两个兴奋性神经元组成；这三个神经元的电路对六条腿的所有运动节奏均必要且充足，并在四个连接组数据集中得到验证。模拟还预测，一个独立的下行通路（DNb08）驱动节奏性腿部运动，我们使用行为果蝇的光遗传学实验予以确认。我们的研究结果揭示了果蝇步行及其他节奏性腿部运动的假设性 CPG 电路的细胞身份和突触结构。基于果蝇连接组的神经网络计算模拟识别出一个三神经元电路，该电路组织用于产生步行的腿部运动节奏。
